notes: Site: Sitecore/.NET store (normann-copenhagen.com), English-first (.com renders /en/ by default, auto geo-redirected to /en/ with USD). Direct HTTP fetch worked throughout (homepage visited first to establish ASP.NET_SessionId/website#lang session cookies per prior access notes for SR147). Checked: main nav (header mega-menu, all levels), footer nav, robots.txt (no Claude-specific disallow), sitemap.xml (returns HTTP 500, unavailable), and site's own search for 'bestseller'/'bestsellers'/'top sellers' (0 hits each - confirms landing pages aren't search-indexed, not proof of absence, so also probed direct URLs). Main nav has no 'Bestsellers' entry. Probed URL guesses: /en/bestsellers/ resolved to REAL distinct content (200, title='Bestsellers | Normann Copenhagen', og:url matches); /en/best-sellers/ (hyphenated), /en/products/bestsellers, /en/products/best-sellers all resolve to the site's soft-404 fallback (either a styled '404_NotFound'/'PAGE NOT FOUND' page or a bare homepage-content fallback, both distinguishable by byte-size/title from the real bestsellers page) - confirms /en/bestsellers/ is the one genuine URL. Opened and inspected /en/bestsellers/ in full: it is NOT built on the site's standard category-tree PLP template (which has a data-totalhits counter, breadcrumb, filter/sort, and CustomSearch/GetResultsAjax pagination - confirmed present on genuine category pages like /en/products/lighting/pendants/ per prior pass). Instead it consists of 5 separate 3-item horizontal 'spotlist' carousel widgets (class 'relatedproductshorizontallist spotlist', same widget markup normally used for 'related products' on other page types), no pagination, no product-count element, and empty on-page h1/h2 title elements (only the <title> tag and og:title metadata literally say 'Bestsellers'). The 15 products shown are genuinely distinct (verified no duplicate hrefs) and span multiple unrelated categories (furniture, lighting, tableware, kitchen, hooks, mirrors, objects), consistent with a manually curated cross-category 'top sellers' spotlight rather than a generic single-category related-items widget. Treated as one valid Bestsellers row per the URL/title/metadata being an explicit, deliberate site label, with qty derived from an exhaustive manual count of all product tiles on the (unpaginated) page - flagged for manual review given the non-standard structure.

Products are genuinely distinct and cross-category, consistent with real curation, but please confirm this isn't a generic/fallback related-products widget rather than a deliberate merchandising bestsellers page.
